changes: Conversations flow better: if the next part of a conversation fits below the text already on screen, it appears there instead of on a fresh panel.
The weapon and armour shops show both lists at the top. Press Left or Right to switch between Weapons and Armour.
Every piece of equipment in a shop shows its status: EQUIPPED, UPGRADE, NO UPGRADE (yours is as good or better) or NEED GOLD. Choosing one you can't buy tells you why.
Shop lists have OWNED and PRICE columns, so you can see how many of an item you already carry. The count also shows while you buy, and updates right after a purchase.
Continue after Game Over: retry a lost battle from exactly where it started, with the items you used back in your bag and Mace taking the first turn. Or choose Back to title.
A new game shows the first chapter card before the village appears, with its chapter music.
Changing scenes (areas, battles, chapter cards) no longer flashes the old picture in the new scene's colours.
Title screen: the light rays behind the logo are gone, leaving the golden logo over a glowing sun.
A new title screen: the redrawn Avalon logo in gold, fading in from black, with the title music.
All menus use the same compact font as the status panel.
Shops show your gold in the corner of the panel, and the new amount right after a purchase.
New intro artwork: the village panorama from Avalon: Legacy Edition and a newly drawn Mace.
The redrawn Mace portrait in the status, dialogue and battle panels.
The music choice under Options on the title screen is steadier: moving through the list no longer redraws it, and cancelling keeps the current sound card.
Smoother menus: moving the cursor in the save, load and other menus only redraws the cursor, not the whole menu.
Runs on ASCII16-X flash cartridges, and saves all five slots and the settings in the cartridge's own flash memory (ON-CARTRIDGE FLASH). No FM-PAC or disk needed.
Emulators and loaders recognise the cartridge as ASCII16 automatically.
Fixed the White Tower console and its font.
Safer hardware detection at startup, for MSX-MUSIC, FM-PAC and SCC on expanded slots.
Fixed saving to an FM-PAC.
Fixes from testing on real MSX machines: the title screen border stays black, and Load Game shows SAVED or EMPTY for all five slots.
No more hanging notes while saving, loading or entering a new area.
More ways to save: choose cartridge SRAM, an FM-PAC or a disk in drive A, then one of five slots. Your Options are saved too.
Choose the music under Options: MoonSound, MSX-MUSIC, MSX-AUDIO, both together in stereo, SCC+ or off. Only the sound cards you have are offered.
Drums play in stereo on MSX-MUSIC and MSX-AUDIO together, and several songs were improved.
An improved title screen.
Startup logos: the original MiG logo and the Seven Mages logo, each with its own PSG sound. Press a key to skip them.
The battle selection grid lines up with the status box below it.
First release of Avalon MSX.
